T2d initial implementation (Y6 発注): MLS-MPM (P2G -> grid update -> G2P, quadratic B-spline kernel, APIC/MLS-MPM affine transfer, Hu et al. 2018 structure) implemented in CPU TypeScript rather than WebGPU compute (T2d-mpm.md's explicitly-permitted fallback; see README Setup for why). New self-contained state representation for this Study: MpmParticle[] (position/velocity/deformation-gradient F/affine-velocity C/mass/volume0), seeded from S1 balls by per-ball rejection sampling (seeding.ts). Constitutive law is the phase knob (T2d-mpm.md core requirement): Cauchy stress blends a real compressible Neo-Hookean solid (mu/lambda from Young's modulus E and Poisson's ratio nu) with a real weakly-compressible viscous fluid (linear EOS pressure from bulk modulus K, viscous term from the APIC C matrix as a velocity-gradient proxy) -- both SVD-free by design (see README for the SVD-based alternative considered and rejected). F itself is separately blended toward its isotropic (volume-only) form by phase, so the fluid end loses shape memory. History ops: seed/setParam/run/freeze/clear; freeze carries the frozen Ball[] result explicitly in its args (T2d-mpm.md's confirmed design, unlike sag.ts's implicit-recompute freeze) so replay never depends on whether a future revisit swaps CPU for GPU. Freeze bins particles into a coarse spatial grid and turns each populated bin into one equal-volume ball (seeding.ts's freezeParticlesToBalls), exportable as an S1-format recipe (serializeFrozenAsS1Recipe) -- verified round-tripping into S1's own importJson with byte-identical ball data. Autorun (continuous simulation) advances physics every animation frame directly but only appends ONE consolidated `run` history entry when toggled off, to avoid flooding history (main.ts's flushAutoRun) -- verified this doesn't double-apply physics and that export/import after a flush reproduces the exact same particle state. Point-cloud renderer (THREE.Points, phase-tinted color, not a calibrated 余白 instrument per Y6's role separation). Verified in isolated Chrome (port 5185) via window.__mpm: all 6 completion conditions hold, including a genuine elastic bounce (solid end: height fell to a minimum then rebounded across several run() batches) that sag.ts's fixed-240-iteration damped relaxation solver cannot produce by construction -- used as completion condition 2's 'behavior the spring sketch couldn't show'. Measured performance: gridN=48 (110,592 cells), DT=1/6000s, ~9.3ms/substep at 3,307 particles and ~3.5ms/substep at 1,321 particles in the isolated headless environment; autorun ran at ~8-10fps at 3,307 particles (chunk=8 substeps/frame) -- see README Observation for the full numbers and the honest 'about 56x slower than real time' framing (60fps was explicitly out of scope per T2d-mpm.md).

T2e WebGPU backend (v0.2.0): added src/studies/mpm/gpu/ (capabilities.ts device detection, shaders.ts WGSL -- a line-for-line port of sim.ts's substep() with fixed-point atomic<i32> P2G scatter, gpuSim.ts orchestration). Physics unchanged (same constitutive law, DT, boundary/friction constants as CPU sim.ts) -- a port, not a redesign, per T2e's explicit instruction. CPU backend (sim.ts) kept as both the WebGPU-unavailable fallback and the deterministic verification baseline; backend selection auto-detects at startup (WebGPU preferred when available), is manually switchable via UI radio buttons, is always visible in a persistent on-screen badge, and is explicitly NOT recorded in history (backend is a pure runtime/live concern, history.ts untouched). gridN is now exposed as a UI slider (T2d's carried-over homework). Rendering stays on THREE.WebGLRenderer (no WebGPURenderer migration, per 'やらないこと') with a readback-frequency split: discrete actions (run-once, freeze, backend switch, history export) do a full state readback (position+velocity+F+C, measured 1-13ms across 3k-300k particles) for correctness; continuous autorun reads back positions only every frame (a fraction of that cost) and lazily syncs velocity/F/C via ensureFullGpuSync() when autorun stops or before an action that needs the full state -- this asymmetry was a deliberate, measured choice (README's Setup/Observation), not an accident. Verified via window.__mpm.compareBackends(): CPU vs GPU centroid/energy statistics agree to ~1e-6 relative error on both the solid and fluid ends of the phase knob, using an isolated synthetic seed independent of the live session (not a classic node-based unit test -- this project's established verification convention is a window.__study debug harness exercised in-browser, and WebGPU was confirmed working in this dev environment via navigator.gpu, so the T2e fallback plan of 'compile-only, no execution' wasn't needed). Measured a real GPU/CPU speedup of ~64x at 3,307 particles (0.173ms vs 11.06ms per substep) and confirmed the compute pipeline scales to 300k particles at 4.4ms/substep on this dev machine (Apple Metal-3 adapter) -- full perf table with 3k/30k/100k/300k rows is in README, author-machine (M4 MacBook Air / RTX 3080) rows left blank pending the author's own measurement. All UI interactivity re-verified with REAL coordinate clicks (not synthetic element.click(), per AGENTS §3's 2026-07-10 revision) across both backends: seed, run, autorun on/off, freeze, backend switch, gridN slider, history export/import round-trip, clear -- CPU-path non-regression explicitly confirmed. Found and fixed three WebGPU binding bugs during implementation (all silent GPU-validation failures, not JS exceptions, surfaced via pushErrorScope after compareBackends() showed exactly-zero GPU velocities): P2G exceeded the WebGPU-guaranteed maxStorageBuffersPerShaderStage minimum of 8 (fixed by moving the params buffer from storage to uniform, which doesn't count against that limit); atomic<i32> storage bindings were declared 'read' when WGSL requires atomics to always be 'read_write' even for atomicLoad-only use; a debug-only grid readback helper copied from a buffer missing COPY_SRC usage. Also found and left only partially explained: GPU-backend autorun throughput in THIS dev/verification environment (Electron-embedded headless Chrome) drops drastically (~0.4 chunks/sec) when the WebGL render loop runs concurrently with per-frame WebGPU readback, despite an isolated (no-renderer) harness measuring 60 chunks/sec for the identical GPU call pattern -- mitigated by enlarging the GPU autorun chunk size (8->up to 200 substeps/frame) to amortize the per-readback round-trip, but the underlying contention is undiagnosed and needs verification on the author's native-browser machine (README's Observation and Next have the full writeup; the explicit run-once/freeze/export paths are unaffected and fast).

Fixed a staging-buffer race found on the author's RTX3080: per-frame position readback (autorun) and full readback (freeze) shared staging buffers and could mapAsync concurrently ('already mapped'). All readbacks are now serialized through an internal promise chain in GpuMpmSim. Also: freeze failures now alert instead of failing silently, and the frozen-export button state is synced at startup.

T2f STL import (v0.3.0): new src/studies/mpm/stlImport.ts parses binary STL (80-byte header + uint32 triangle count + 50 bytes/triangle, little-endian -- the exact inverse of cloud-sculpt/meshExport.ts's encodeBinaryStl) and voxel-fills the mesh's interior directly into this Study's own material points -- no sphere-fitting or medial-axis extraction (that stays freeze's job), per the author's 'least implementation effort' instruction (T2f-import-stl.md). Import normalizes the mesh first (uniform-scale longest bbox edge to 60% of DOMAIN_SIZE, center x/z at the domain origin, rest the lowest point just above marginWorld(gridN) -- same convention as main.ts's liftAboveGround for S1 balls), then classifies grid points at spacing h=particlesPerUnitVolume^(-1/3) as inside/outside via a +X ray-parity test (classic point-in-polyhedron; ray-triangle intersection is Möller-Trumbore 1997, specialized to direction (1,0,0)). A hard cap (MAX_MESH_PARTICLES=20000, extrapolated from the existing perf table) triggers deterministic stride-thinning with total mass conserved via the pre-thinning volume estimate, never a silent partial import. New history op 'seedMesh' (history.ts) -- not layered onto the existing 'seed' op because 'seed' always RE-SAMPLES particles from a Ball[] source via seedParticlesFromBalls, which a mesh import has no equivalent of; 'seedMesh' instead carries its OWN filled particle positions explicitly in its args (same 'carry the result, not the recipe for it' pattern as 'freeze' carrying its Ball[] result), so replay never needs the original STL triangle data. ASCII STL is explicitly declined (not supported) with a clear error message asking for a binary re-export, disambiguated from binary STLs that happen to also start with 'solid ...' header text by checking the file's byte length against the binary format's own size formula, not just the text. New UI: an 'STLを取り込む' file input in the seeding section plus a permanent honesty hint about binary-only support and ray-parity's known failure mode on non-watertight meshes (holes can misclassify inside/outside -- no repair or watertight check is attempted, that stays Blender's job). Verified end-to-end in isolated Chrome (port 5185): imported a real self-generated test input (S1's own STL export format, 139,600 triangles, built the same way cloud-sculpt/meshExport.ts's encodeBinaryStl does) in 173ms producing 6,302 correctly-normalized particles; the full 'S1 -> STL -> S2c import -> freeze -> S1 recipe -> S1 import -> re-export STL' round trip stayed watertight (0 open/non-manifold edges) end to end -- the concrete proof that RESEARCH.md's §3 'import existing meshes' promise now closes; liquid-phase run-then-freeze on the same imported particles also worked; history export/import reproduced the imported particle configuration bit-exactly (max diff 0 across 6,302 particles); the particle cap and its mass-conserving thinning were exercised directly (25,245 candidates thinned to exactly 20,000); CPU-backend import/run/freeze was confirmed as a non-regression check alongside WebGPU. UI verification note: the preview_click tool malfunctioned in this session (dispatching clicks at coordinates far outside the emulated viewport, confirmed via a window click-event logger), so interactivity was instead verified via AGENTS §3's explicitly-sanctioned alternative -- document.elementFromPoint hit-testing to confirm no element covers a control, followed by a real trusted-style pointerdown/mousedown/pointerup/mouseup/click event sequence dispatched on the hit-tested element (deliberately not element.click(), which bypasses hit-testing) -- covering both the new STL/S1-recipe file inputs and a non-regression pass over every existing control (seed, run, autorun toggle-with-flush, freeze, backend switch, clear).
